Harappan script - nature, direction, decipherment, signs

accepted.s: Which Harappan feature is associated with the later Hindu conception of Shiva as Pashupati?
accepted.x: The Harappan Pashupati figure is regarded as a possible antecedent of the later Hindu representation of Shiva as Pashupati.
accepted.tq: Use the direct continuity between an archaeological feature and its later religious form.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Linga and yoni stones — Linga worship
accepted.x: The swastika is associated with the auspicious symbol of later times. Fire altars, rather than the swastika, are linked—though debatably—to Vedic yajna.
accepted.tq: Find the mismatched continuity by separating religious symbols from ritual practices.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harappan religious continuities:
1. The Great Bath is associated with the later practice of ritual bathing.
2. Fire altars at Kalibangan are definitively proved to be Vedic yajna sites.
3. Mother Goddess worship has a later parallel in Shakti or mother-goddess cults.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The association of Kalibangan fire altars with Vedic yajna remains debated and is not definitive.
accepted.tq: Reject an absolute claim when an archaeological interpretation is explicitly debated.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes a major contrast between Rig Vedic religion and Harappan religious indications?
o: Rig Vedic religion was centred on male nature gods and open-air yajnas, whereas Harappan religion shows fertility and nature-oriented elements.
Rig Vedic religion was fertility-oriented, whereas Harappan religion was exclusively sacrificial and priest-led.
Rig Vedic religion was centred on temple idols, whereas Harappans had no religious practices.
Rig Vedic religion worshipped animals, whereas Harappans exclusively worshipped male deities.
accepted.x: Rig Vedic religion featured male nature gods such as Indra, Agni and Varuna and open-air yajnas, with no temples or idols. Harappan religion is generally viewed as nature- and fertility-oriented.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into deity type, ritual form and religious orientation.

accepted.s: The Dancing Girl of the Indus Valley Civilization was made of:
accepted.x: The Dancing Girl from Mohenjodaro is a bronze figure produced by the lost-wax or cire perdue method.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive material associated with the famous artefact.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Artefact)
A. Priest-King
B. Nude male torso
C. Dog chasing a deer
D. Copper dog and bird

List-II (Site)
I. Lothal
II. Harappa
III. Mohenjodaro

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Priest-King is from Mohenjodaro; the nude male torso and dog chasing a deer are from Harappa; and the copper dog and bird are from Lothal.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure site pair and eliminate codes with repeated or misplaced locations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Dog chasing a deer — Red sandstone
accepted.x: The Priest-King, a bearded figure with a fillet and trefoil shawl, was made of steatite. The nude male torso was made of red sandstone, the dog chasing a deer of bronze, and the bull figure of Kalibangan of bronze.
accepted.tq: Use material-based discrimination among closely related Harappan artefacts.

accepted.s: The bull figure associated with Kalibangan was made of:
accepted.x: The bull figure from Kalibangan is identified as a bronze artefact.
accepted.tq: Recall the artefact–material pair rather than the site alone.

accepted.s: A horned deity incised on a cake found at Kalibangan was made on:
accepted.x: The horned deity was incised on a terracotta cake from Kalibangan.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the material of an engraved object from the metals used for figurines.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dancing Girl:
1. It was excavated in 1926 by Ernest Mackay under John Marshall.
2. It belongs to the Mature Harappan phase.
3. It is dated approximately to 2500 BCE.
4. Its right hand is placed on the hip and its left arm is covered with bangles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the Dancing Girl: its excavation, phase, approximate date and distinctive posture and ornaments.
accepted.tq: Treat date, excavator, period and physical features as separate factual clues.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Harappan buildings and polity is correct?
o: Fortified citadels prove that the cities were governed exclusively by warriors.
Planned cities and drainage systems suggest some form of municipal governance.
Large palaces and temples have been conclusively identified in all major cities.
The political system is conclusively known to have been a hereditary monarchy.
accepted.x: Planned cities and drains suggest municipal governance, while the exact political structure remains uncertain. Citadels may indicate a ruling group, but its composition is debated.
accepted.tq: Choose the cautious inference supported by urban planning rather than an unproved political claim.
accepted.sec: Palaces and temples - secular or religious, classes, polity

accepted.s:
With reference to the Indus Valley Civilization, consider the following statements:
1. It was predominantly secular, although religion was present.
2. Horse-drawn chariots are clearly evidenced in Harappan warfare.
3. A four-fold social division into scholars, warriors, traders and labourers is firmly established.
4. Differences in house size, burial goods and ornaments indicate social stratification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. No horse-drawn chariots have been found as clear evidence of Harappan warfare, and the proposed four-fold division is speculative.
accepted.tq: Separate archaeological evidence from speculative reconstruction of social classes.
accepted.sec: Palaces and temples - secular or religious, classes, polity

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains the status of the so-called ruling group in Harappan cities?
o: It is conclusively identified as a military aristocracy through royal inscriptions.
It consisted exclusively of temple priests because temples have been found in the citadels.
The fortified citadel may indicate a ruling group, possibly priestly or merchant, but the interpretation is debated.
It was absent because Harappan cities had no political organisation.
accepted.x: Fortified citadels suggest the presence of some ruling group, but its nature—possibly priestly or merchant—is not conclusively established.
accepted.tq: Prefer the qualified archaeological interpretation over an exclusive identification.
accepted.sec: Palaces and temples - secular or religious, classes, polity

accepted.s: The dominant Harappan pottery type was:
o: White glazed ware with blue designs
Red ware with black painted designs
Black ware with red geometric designs
Yellow ware with green floral designs
accepted.x: Harappan pottery was predominantly red ware decorated with black painted designs. Plain red ware was also common.
accepted.tq: Recall the dominant colour–design combination directly.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a common motif on Harappan painted pottery?
accepted.x: Geometric, floral, pipal leaf and fish-scale motifs are associated with Harappan pottery. Human royal portraits are not listed as a common painted motif.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider from a cluster of documented decorative motifs.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan pottery:
1. It was generally made on the potter’s wheel.
2. Glazed pottery is associated with the Harappan civilization.
3. Kalibangan yielded six types of pottery.
4. Harappa had reserved slip ware of Mesopotamian type.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Harappan pottery was wheel-made, included glazed pottery, and showed the specified regional varieties at Kalibangan and Harappa.
accepted.tq: Combine production method, technological feature and site-specific varieties before selecting the coded option.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Harappan script?
o: It is pictographic, contains about 40 signs and was deciphered through bilingual inscriptions.
It is alphabetic, contains about 40 signs and has been fully deciphered.
It is syllabic, contains about 4,000 signs and was written only vertically.
It is pictographic, contains about 400 signs and remains undeciphered.
accepted.x: The Harappan script is pictographic, has approximately 400 signs and remains undeciphered.
accepted.tq: Use the three-part combination of nature, number and decipherment status.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - nature, direction, decipherment, signs

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Dholavira signboard carries ten signs. Boustrophedon writing is associated with Kalibangan, the fish is the commonest sign, and the script remains undeciphered.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive script feature to the correct site.
accepted.sec: Harappan script - nature, direction, decipherment, signs

accepted.s: Which of the following was a known Harappan toy or game object?
accepted.x: Terracotta carts, whistles, rattles, birds, animals, gamesmen and discs are among the known Harappan toys and game objects. Dice have been found at Harappa.
accepted.tq: Select the archaeological object from the documented toy assemblage.

accepted.s: At which Harappan site has lipstick been identified?
accepted.x: Lipstick has been identified at Chanhudaro. Mirrors and combs, along with varied hair and beard styles, indicate awareness of personal grooming and fashion.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive cosmetic–site association.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Harappan personal adornment and clothing:
1. Ornaments were made of gold, silver, beads and shell.
2. Shell bangles were used.
3. Cotton and wool were among the clothing materials.
4. Mirrors and combs were unknown to the Harappans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Mirrors and combs were known, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed claim inserted into an otherwise factual list.

accepted.s: Which of the following best expresses the historical significance of Harappan religious evidence?
o: It demonstrates that Harappan religion was exclusively based on Vedic sacrifice.
It provides early material evidence of cults involving a Shiva-like deity, a mother goddess and linga-related symbols that later show continuities.
It proves that the later Hindu religious system already existed in its complete form.
It establishes that all Harappan symbols had one fixed and universally accepted meaning.
accepted.x: Harappan artefacts provide early material evidence of cultic elements that may have continued into later Hinduism. They do not prove that later Hinduism existed in a complete form or that every symbol has a certain interpretation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish historical continuity from the claim of complete identity.

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The identification of the Pashupati seal as a proto-Shiva representation is treated cautiously.
Reason (R): The Harappan script remains undeciphered and the religious interpretation of the seal is therefore not conclusively established.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the undeciphered nature of Harappan records is a principal reason why the proto-Shiva interpretation remains debated rather than proven.
accepted.tq: Check whether the reason directly accounts for the cautious status of the interpretation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares Harappan religion with Later Vedic religion?
o: Harappan religion was exclusively priest-led, whereas Later Vedic religion rejected sacrifice.
Harappan religion rejected fertility symbolism, whereas Later Vedic religion centred on mother-goddess cults.
Harappan religion was nature- and fertility-oriented, whereas Later Vedic religion was sacrificial and priest-led.
Both were identical in their ritual system and religious leadership.
accepted.x: Harappan religious indications are associated with nature and fertility, while Later Vedic religion was more sacrificial and priest-led.
accepted.tq: Compare the dominant orientation and ritual leadership of the two traditions.

accepted.s: Gudimallam, associated with the Satavahana era, is noted in Andhra Pradesh for:
o: The earliest known Buddhist stupa in India
The first Harappan fire altar in South India
The oldest Shaivite temple in Andhra Pradesh and a very early Shiva lingam
accepted.x: Gudimallam is described as having the oldest Shaivite temple in Andhra Pradesh and as representing the first Shiva lingam in Andhra Pradesh and India in the cited tradition.
accepted.tq: Use the AP-specific cultural association and distinguish it from Indus archaeological features.

accepted.s: Which of the following recent developments is correctly associated with Rakhigarhi?
o: It yielded the Dancing Girl made of bronze and excavated by John Marshall.
It is the only site where the Harappan script has been deciphered.
It is the only Harappan site associated with ancient DNA and has evidence of a gold foundry and gemstone factory.
It contains the Great Bath and the largest known Harappan signboard.
accepted.x: Rakhigarhi is noted as the only Harappan site with ancient DNA in the cited account, along with evidence of a gold foundry and gemstone factory.
accepted.tq: Link the site to its distinctive scientific and craft-production evidence.

accepted.s: A rare cylindrical steatite seal bearing an alligator motif and five Harappan signs has been associated with:
accepted.x: The rare cylindrical steatite seal with an alligator motif and five Harappan signs is associated with Rakhigarhi.
accepted.tq: Use the unusual motif and sign count as a high-value identification clue.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the proposed ‘priest-king’ identification is correct?
o: It is conclusively established by a contemporary Harappan inscription naming the ruler.
It was a title used by Later Vedic kings.
It is an interpretive label and is not proven.
It refers to a terracotta toy found at Kalibangan.
accepted.x: The label ‘priest-king’ applied to the bearded Mohenjodaro figure is an interpretation, not a proven identification supported by a deciphered inscription.
accepted.tq: Reject a famous but unproven label when the evidence is interpretive.
